title: Windows: editor leaks ~1000 GDI objects per project run when single_window_mode is off, breaking all window creation after 10+ runs
body:
# Editor leaks ~1000 GDI objects per game run cycle when multi-window mode is off (Godot 4.7.2)

## System Info
- Godot: v4.7.2.stable.steam
- OS: Windows 11 (26H2, build 26100)
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX 5070 Laptop GPU, driver 573.24 (2025-05)
- Editor setting: `interface/editor/display/single_window_mode = false` (multi-window mode, which is the default on fresh install)

## Problem Description

Every time the current project is run from the editor (press F5), the **editor process** leaks approximately 700–1000 GDI objects. The game itself starts successfully and plays normally, but the leaked GDI objects are never released by the editor when the game stops.

After 10–15 F5 run/stop cycles, the editor exhausts the Windows per-process GDI object limit (10,000). At that point:
- Output panel floods with `Failed to create Windows OS window` / `INVALID_WINDOW_ID` errors
- F5 stops working (no game window appears)
- The editor can still edit scenes/scripts, but cannot create any popup dialogs or sub-windows
- Restarting the editor resets GDI count to ~31 and the cycle repeats

## Reproduction Steps

1. Create or open any 2D project (tested with empty scene + one `CharacterBody2D`).
2. Start monitoring editor GDI usage:
   ```powershell
   Add-Type -TypeDefinition @"
   using System;
   using System.Runtime.InteropServices;
   public class G {
     [DllImport("user32.dll")] public static extern uint GetGuiResources(IntPtr h, uint f);
   }
   "@
   $p = Get-Process | Where-Object { $_.ProcessName -match "godot" } | Select-Object -First 1
   while ($p) {
     $gdi = [G]::GetGuiResources($p.Handle, 1)
     Write-Host "$(Get-Date -Format 'HH:mm:ss') PID=$($p.Id) GDI=$gdi"
     Start-Sleep 5
     $p = Get-Process | Where-Object { $_.ProcessName -match "godot" } | Select-Object -First 1
   }
   ```
3. Press F5 → wait for game window to appear → close game.
4. Repeat step 3 five or more times.
5. Observe: editor GDI count increases monotonically with each cycle.

## Measured Data (20-second sampling interval)

```
20:09:42  Editor start (PID=35700)                GDI=31
20:13:02  Before F5                               GDI=30
20:13:22  Game running (PID=29796, GDI=31)        Editor GDI=281  ← +250
20:13:42  Game stopped                            Editor GDI=981  ← +700 net leak
   
20:15:42  After 2nd F5 cycle                      Editor GDI=1243
20:16:02  Editor GDI=1869                         ← +626
   
20:22:23  After 3rd F5 cycle                      Editor GDI=4142  ← ~1450 per cycle
   
~15 more cycles later (GDI hits 10,000 cap):
20:06:02  Editor GDI=10000 (capped)
          F5 now produces:
            ERROR: platform/windows/display_server_windows.cpp:3600 - Condition "!windows.has(p_window)" is true. Returning: FAILED
            ERROR: Failed to create Windows OS window.
            ERROR: Failed to create sub window.
            ERROR: scene/main/window.cpp:727 - Condition "window_id == DisplayServerEnums::INVALID_WINDOW_ID" is true.
            ERROR: platform/windows/display_server_windows.cpp:2250 - Condition "!windows.has(p_window)" is true. Returning: DisplayServerEnums::INVALID_SCREEN
          Game window never appears.
```

**Key observation**: GDI does **not** leak during normal scene editing (verified 4+ minutes of editing scenes/scripts: GDI stayed 31–33, no growth). The leak only happens when running the project.

## Workaround Verified

Enabling `interface/editor/display/single_window_mode = true` (Editor Settings → Interface → Editor → Display → Single Window Mode, restart editor) **completely eliminates the leak**:

```
20:22:43  Editor start (PID=37008, single_window_mode=on)  GDI=31
20:22:52  Game running (PID=31528)                         Editor GDI=31  ← no leak
20:23:03  Game stopped                                     Editor GDI=31  ← stable
20:26:23  After another F5 cycle                           Editor GDI=50  ← tiny drift (~19 over 10 cycles)
```

GDI remained <55 throughout the session in single-window mode.

## Related Issues

- **#114496** "GDI object leak on Windows with embed_subwindows = false" — closed by PR #114525 in 4.6. That issue involved **project setting** `window/subwindows/embed_subwindows` (affecting `Window` nodes inside a running game). This report concerns the **editor process** itself leaking GDI when spawning/destroying the game window during F5, tied to the **editor setting** `single_window_mode`. The root cause may be in a different code path (display server window creation from editor side vs. game-side window nodes).
- **PR #114525** fixed `WM_SETICON` handle management in `display_server_windows.cpp` for game window nodes. This may be a separate leak in the editor's game-launching flow.

## Expected Behavior

The editor's GDI object count should remain stable across F5 run/stop cycles, or the leaked GDI objects should be properly released when the game window is destroyed.

## Actual Behavior

The editor accumulates ~1000 GDI objects per run/stop cycle when `single_window_mode = false`, eventually causing complete failure of all window-creating operations.

## Additional Context

- Only **GDI** objects leak; USER objects, kernel handles, and memory remain stable.
- The game process itself never exceeds ~32 GDI objects and runs normally.
- Leak persists in Godot 4.7.2 despite fix in #114525 targeting 4.6.
- (Not tested whether the leak also occurs with the Forward+ project renderer; the measurements above were taken with a Compatibility-renderer project.)
